classification.difficultyReason: Verify a logistic model by differentiation and substitution, then interpret its initial population, limiting population and relative growth rate.

content.prompt:
A kangaroo population is modelled by
$$K=\frac{12\,000}{4+e^{-t/4}}$$
where $t$ is years from today.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}K&=12\,000(4+e^{-t/4})^{-1}\\\frac{dK}{dt}&=12\,000(-1)(4+e^{-t/4})^{-2}\left(-\frac14e^{-t/4}\right)\\&=\frac{3000e^{-t/4}}{(4+e^{-t/4})^2}.\end{align*}$$
Check by substitution:
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{RHS}&=\frac14\left(\frac{12\,000}{4+e^{-t/4}}\right)\left(1-\frac{\frac{12\,000}{4+e^{-t/4}}}{3000}\right)\\&=\frac14\left(\frac{12\,000}{4+e^{-t/4}}\right)\left(1-\frac4{4+e^{-t/4}}\right)\\&=\frac14\left(\frac{12\,000}{4+e^{-t/4}}\right)\left(\frac{4+e^{-t/4}-4}{4+e^{-t/4}}\right)\\&=\frac14\left(\frac{12\,000}{4+e^{-t/4}}\right)\left(\frac{e^{-t/4}}{4+e^{-t/4}}\right)\\&=\frac{3000e^{-t/4}}{(4+e^{-t/4})^2}\\&=\mathrm{LHS}.\end{align*}$$
Thus $K$ satisfies the differential equation.

Today, $t=0$:
$$\begin{align*}K(0)&=\frac{12\,000}{4+1}\\&=2400.\end{align*}$$
The population today is 2400 kangaroos.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What eventual population does the model predict?

answer.worked:
As $t\to\infty$, $e^{-t/4}\to0$, so
$$K\to\frac{12\,000}{4}=3000.$$
The model predicts an eventual population of 3000 kangaroos.

children.label: d
children.prompt: What is the annual percentage growth rate today?

answer.worked:
At $t=0$, $K=2400$:
$$\begin{align*}\left.\frac{dK}{dt}\right|_{t=0}&=\frac14(2400)\left(1-\frac{2400}{3000}\right)\\&=120\text{ kangaroos per year}.\end{align*}$$
$$\text{Percentage growth rate}=\frac{120}{2400}\times100\%=5\%\text{ per year}.$$
